one_line: Agent-discoverable storefront for inspecting and previewing services before human-controlled purchase.
what_it_does: Exposes find, inspect, preview, and purchase operations for a service catalog, with synthetic dry-run receipts and human purchase control.
leverage_rationale: Structured, page-scoped contracts make service discovery and exact inspection substantially more reliable than UI guessing; purchase remains deliberately human-controlled.
leverage_evidence: About text names four page-scoped tools: find_services, get_service, preview_service, buy_service.
Frame evidence visibly shows the catalog and PAGE-SCOPED WEBMCP panel with those operations.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently describes a scoped marketplace and a concrete PO Match Gate flow, but the submitted frames show setup/discovery rather than a completed preview or purchase.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive and a concrete PO Match Gate listing is visible in frame evidence.
About text explicitly labels preview as a dry run recording a receipt, not fresh model inference.
impact_rationale: Service creators and buyers have a credible need to discover exact contracts and safely evaluate automated services before purchase.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets service discovery, contract understanding, previews, and human purchase decisions.
creativity_rationale: The service marketplace treats WebMCP as a stable catalog capability surface rather than one tool per listing, with explicit untrusted catalog text and preview semantics.
creativity_evidence: About text describes a constant tool set as the catalog grows and distinguishes read-only discovery from durable preview writes.
usability_note: Catalog/search UI is legible in the frame evidence; end-to-end completion is not shown.
red_flags: No completed tool response, preview receipt, or purchase result is visible in the submitted frame sheets.
standouts: Clear separation of agent discovery/inspection from human purchase control.
Honest dry-run labeling and bounded/untrusted catalog treatment.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP-specific marketplace concept with a live-looking product and coherent safety boundary, despite incomplete end-to-end evidence.

one_line: Agent-readable travel itinerary with structured day and rain-backup retrieval tools.
what_it_does: Exposes authoritative trip summary, day itinerary, and rainy-day backup data to agents without requiring UI scraping.
leverage_rationale: Structured itinerary retrieval improves grounding and precision, though the product is primarily a read-only itinerary that a general agent could scrape with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies get_trip_summary, get_day_itinerary, and get_rain_backup.
Frame evidence shows a populated multi-day itinerary interface.
execution_rationale: The itinerary UI and tool concept are coherent, but the packet does not evidence an actual agent query or returned backup result end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive.
Frame sheet visibly shows day-by-day itinerary content and a consistent application layout.
impact_rationale: Travelers have a concrete need for reliable itinerary retrieval and context-aware contingency planning such as rain backups.
impact_evidence: Concrete tomorrow-afternoon rain scenario is described.
Site-provided data is explicitly preferred over invented business names.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native itinerary grounding is a useful, thoughtful synthesis, but the interaction model is a relatively direct application of structured read tools.
creativity_evidence: About text frames the site as an existing trip made readable and adaptable for agents rather than generated by them.
usability_note: Visual itinerary appears organized and readable; actual agent interaction is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No visible tool invocation or returned rain-backup result in the frame evidence.
standouts: Explicitly avoids hallucinating a specific backup business when the itinerary only contains a generic intention.
advance_reason: Clear, credible agent-grounding use case with a coherent live-looking itinerary, though evidence is read-only and incomplete.

one_line: Adaptive Live Canvas that lets agents compose bounded storefront, dashboard, and reporting interfaces.
what_it_does: Provides constrained agent composition areas for curating search results, generating dashboards, and creating browser-local reports.
leverage_rationale: The core product is the agent-composed interface itself; WebMCP changes the UI from fixed pages into a bounded, persistent composition surface that general UI driving cannot replicate comparably.
leverage_evidence: About text describes a bounded WebMCP Live Canvas for agent redesign.
Scope spans approved storefront components, blank dashboards, and distributable datatable/report components.
execution_rationale: The packet presents three coherent demos and a clear safety constraint, but the available evidence is primarily descriptive and does not show a completed composition result clearly.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive.
About text specifies distinct storefront, dashboard, and distribution demos with bounded composition.
impact_rationale: Personalized shopping research, CRM/ERP dashboards, and bespoke reports address substantial usability and workflow needs for distinct audiences.
impact_evidence: About text identifies open-cart research friction and dashboard/report personalization use cases.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-UI through safe agent composition is an unusually ambitious interaction model pursued across multiple product surfaces.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly asks what the web would be if users could bring their own interface.
Approved presets and browser-local report generation extend the idea beyond a chat layer.
usability_note: Ambitious multi-demo concept; packet evidence does not establish how easily users control or recover compositions.
red_flags: Broad scope and sparse observable end-to-end evidence make completeness difficult to verify.
standouts: Bounded composition is a strong response to untrusted public-web content.
Same concept is demonstrated across storefront, dashboard, and component-distribution contexts.
advance_reason: Highly original and WebMCP-central concept with credible impact across several workflows; advance despite limited completion evidence.

one_line: Personal saved-content library exposed to agents for retrieval and saving.
what_it_does: Lets an agent search and retrieve a user's saved links and save new content through a browser-native personal library.
leverage_rationale: Agent access to private saved context without plugins, API-key sharing, or configuration is central to the stated retrieval experience.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly exposes search, retrieve, and save as WebMCP tools.
About text identifies retrieval of saved articles, posts, videos, and threads as the core problem.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad product with many surfaces, but no frame sheet was submitted and the available packaging evidence is insufficient to verify the central workflow.
execution_evidence: Eight gallery images are reported, but no video frame sheets were submitted.
About text lists dashboard, extension, chat import, RAG chat, and marketplace surfaces.
impact_rationale: People who save large amounts of content have a clear retrieval problem, and agent search over personal context directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text gives a specific recurring frustration: saved links and tabs become a graveyard and are rarely revisited.
Product is positioned as retrieval rather than merely faster saving.
creativity_rationale: A personal library made natively accessible to any agent is a useful and timely interaction shift, though the underlying bookmark category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: No-plugin, no-API-key-sharing agent access is a distinctive product framing.
usability_note: Many listed surfaces suggest breadth, but no frame sheet is available to assess flow quality.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets; central product behavior cannot be visually checked.
Very broad feature list relative to available evidence.
standouts: Targets retrieval—the neglected half of bookmarking—with agent-native personal context.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable and WebMCP-relevant, but the packet lacks sufficient observable execution evidence for advancement.

one_line: Voice-first flight search concept intended to make booking independently accessible to visually impaired users.
what_it_does: Uses an agent to translate complex flight search into conversational audio and high-contrast results.
leverage_rationale: A structured agent surface paired with voice output can remove visual UI navigation, especially for screen-reader users, but the packet does not verify the live data flow.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on bypassing cluttered flight websites through a voice-first agent.
About text claims dynamic WebMCP flight-data discovery and simplified audio output.
execution_rationale: The accessibility goal is coherent, but demo_alive is unknown and no frame sheets were submitted, so the claimed flight search and audio result cannot be verified.
execution_evidence: No video frame sheets were submitted.
Demo status is reported unknown; description is the primary evidence.
impact_rationale: Independent flight search is a real, high-value accessibility need for visually impaired and elderly travelers.
impact_evidence: About text identifies screen-reader barriers in calendar widgets, pop-ups, and pricing filters.
Proposed interaction is a single spoken request for a flight.
creativity_rationale: Voice-first, agent-mediated travel search for accessibility is a meaningful and socially valuable synthesis, though the basic travel-agent pattern is known.
creativity_evidence: Claims WCAG AAA-oriented high-contrast text alongside conversational audio.
usability_note: Accessibility intent is strong, but no observable interaction or output is provided.
red_flags: Demo status unknown and no frame/video evidence.
Claims real-time flight data and booking independence without observable proof.
standouts: Specific accessibility audience and barrier rather than generic AI travel convenience.
advance_reason: High potential impact but insufficient evidence that the claimed product and WebMCP flow work.

one_line: Consent-aware agent form filling that reveals only the fields a form actually requires.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect requirements, perform privacy-preserving checks, request allow-listed fields, and apply only human-approved values.
leverage_rationale: Shared live consent state, capability registration/removal, scoped disclosure, and consent-version checks are difficult to reproduce reliably through generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes requirements, missing answers, approved scope, consent version, and review status shared between page and agent.
Age check returns an is_adult boolean rather than DOB; old tool handles fail after revocation.
execution_rationale: The central flow is unusually well specified with approval, revocation, versioning, and no-submit boundary; frame evidence supports the form workflow, though not every state is observable.
execution_evidence: Demo profile has 23 fields while sample form needs five fields plus an age check.
Description states the flow reaches 6/6 requirements after approved values and exposes a local submitted:false packet only after review.
impact_rationale: Privacy-preserving form completion addresses a broad and concrete problem: agents need enough data to complete forms without unrestricted profile access.
impact_evidence: Human approval is required per field and final submission is excluded.
creativity_rationale: Capability-as-consent-version and privacy-preserving boolean checks create a memorable interaction model rather than merely automating form filling.
creativity_evidence: Revocation invalidates prior handles and removes temporary write capability.
The project makes the data boundary visible as its central design goal.
usability_note: The narrow, explicit consent flow is understandable and gives users control; final submission remains intentionally separate.
red_flags: Synthetic local demo and no real external submission; impact is demonstrated as a pattern rather than deployment.
standouts: Strong consent semantics: inspect without disclosure, approve per field, revoke by version.
Explicitly avoids turning a local demo into a claim of real submission.
advance_reason: Best-in-packet combination of WebMCP indispensability, concrete safety mechanics, and coherent evidenced workflow.

one_line: Store-operations console where agents investigate and propose actions while merchants approve exact mutations.
what_it_does: Provides read tools for store data and a validated ticket flow for refunds/cancellations requiring merchant approval and one-time exact execution.
leverage_rationale: Shared approval state, canonical parameter freezing, replay protection, and one-time execution are core agent-human safety mechanics not reliably achieved by generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies agent suggestion → approval → exact parameter match → one-time execution → confirmation.
Fourteen tools cover operational reads while mutations require approved tickets.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a concrete refund scenario plus validation failures and replay protections, with a coherent browser-only implementation; end-to-end visual proof remains limited.
execution_evidence: Guided demo is described for order ORD-1042, including validation failures and mismatched/replayed request protections.
Demo is reported alive and the application is deployed as a React app.
impact_rationale: Merchant operations involve costly, sensitive mutations where reliable agent assistance and human approval have clear practical value.
impact_evidence: Concrete refund/cancel use case and merchant approval boundary.
Reads cover orders, customers, policies, inventory, shipping, products, and sales.
creativity_rationale: The project pursues exact-parameter approval and replay-safe execution as the central product interaction, beyond a generic agent dashboard.
creativity_evidence: Description emphasizes approval of actual amount/order/operation rather than vague future intent.
One-time tickets and canonical parameter matching are explicit design choices.
usability_note: Operational console and explicit approval sequence should be understandable; visual evidence does not fully show completion.
red_flags: All data is in memory and there is no backend/payment integration, limiting production validation.
standouts: Strong mutation-safety boundary with parameter binding and replay prevention.
advance_reason: High WebMCP leverage and credible safety-focused store workflow with concrete evidence and strong ambition.

one_line: Agent-native medication regimen workspace for structured interaction and safety review.
what_it_does: Manages medications, detects potential interactions, presents regimen safety context, and supports caregiver workflows through structured agent access.
leverage_rationale: Structured medication context can improve agent grounding and caregiver workflows, but the packet does not establish that generic automation could not reach similar read outcomes.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text describe structured medication context exposed through WebMCP.
Feature list includes interaction detection, safety score, risk distinctions, and medication search.
execution_rationale: The stated workspace and feature set are coherent, but no frame sheets or video evidence were submitted, so clinical workflow completion is unverified.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and fifteen gallery images exist, but no video frame sheets were submitted.
About text provides a feature list without observable end-to-end result evidence.
impact_rationale: Medication interaction awareness and caregiver support address a consequential safety need for patients managing multiple medicines.
impact_evidence: About text identifies the concrete risk of missing interactions when adding medication.
Target users include patients and caregivers managing regimens.
creativity_rationale: Agent-mediated regimen review is a useful application of structured health data, but the concept is a familiar medication-safety assistant pattern.
creativity_evidence: Human-decides framing and separation of agent investigation from provided medication context.
usability_note: Potentially clear medication workspace, but visual workflow and warnings cannot be assessed from submitted frame evidence.
red_flags: No submitted video frame sheets; safety scores and interaction results are not visually verified.
Health claims require careful grounding and safety disclaimers not established in the packet excerpt.
standouts: Clear patient/caregiver audience and consequential problem.
advance_reason: High potential impact, but observable execution and safety behavior are too thin for advancement.

one_line: Agent-native freelance marketplace for structured discovery, evaluation, shortlisting, and proposal drafts.
what_it_does: Lets clients search jobs/freelancers and assess reputation, while freelancers discover jobs and draft proposals; final submission remains human-controlled.
leverage_rationale: Structured marketplace search and Rails authorization improve reliability over scraping, but the main outcomes remain achievable with a general agent at some friction.
leverage_evidence: About text names eight WebMCP tools for search, reputation, shortlists, and proposal drafts.
Tools use the existing authenticated session and Rails authorization rules.
execution_rationale: The stack and central workflow are coherent, but demo status is unknown and no completed interaction is observable in the packet.
execution_evidence: Rails/PostgreSQL application and live URL are described.
About text clearly separates agent-assisted drafts from human-controlled proposal submission.
impact_rationale: Clients and freelancers have a real matching and proposal-preparation problem that structured marketplace access can reduce.
impact_evidence: Two-sided audience and concrete search/evaluation/draft tasks are specified.
creativity_rationale: Agent support across both sides of a freelance marketplace is a competent synthesis, with limited novelty beyond structured marketplace operations.
creativity_evidence: Human-control boundary for submitting proposals is explicit.
usability_note: Workflow is conceptually clear, but unknown demo health and missing observable completion reduce confidence.
red_flags: Demo status unknown and no usable frame evidence establishing end-to-end behavior.
standouts: Uses existing authenticated session and authorization rather than a separate AI layer.
advance_reason: Credible marketplace concept, but packet evidence is too thin and demo status unknown.

one_line: Pet-care agent that retrieves pet context, finds care options, and saves human-approved care plans.
what_it_does: Exposes pet profile, daily needs, services, products, care-plan saving, and care-plan listing through structured WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: The agent can combine structured profile/needs retrieval with service/product discovery and a persisted care-plan write, while server validation and human approval preserve control.
leverage_evidence: About text lists six tools including get_pet_profile, get_daily_needs, find_pet_services, find_pet_products, save_care_plan, and list_care_plans.
Description states server-side validation, human approval boundary, and persisted workflow.
execution_rationale: The product scope and care-plan workflow are coherent and the live agent deployment is identified, but frame evidence does not conclusively show a full saved-plan result.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and an agent-facing deployment URL is provided.
About text describes the concrete request to build Dojo's care plan and the underlying persisted workflow.
impact_rationale: Pet owners and caregivers have recurring needs around routines, services, products, and coordinated care plans.
impact_evidence: Concrete dog profile and daily-care scenario are described.
Care plans are persisted and listable rather than merely conversational.
creativity_rationale: The combination of pet-specific structured context, agent planning, and human-approved persistence is a fresh and appealing application, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Interaction model explicitly shifts from pages/buttons to agents/capabilities for pet care.
usability_note: Natural-language care-plan framing is accessible; evidence does not show all approval and persistence states.
red_flags: Frame evidence does not establish the complete agent invocation-to-persisted-plan sequence.
standouts: Combines read context, discovery, and a durable validated write in a concrete pet-care workflow.
advance_reason: Coherent live product with meaningful structured workflow and human approval, supported by credible packet evidence.
